proof-statement-integrity.evidence: markovTrace_branching had the branching identity as the class field ctx.markovTrace_branching and its body returned that field - 3b-cond item 5 - under docstrings asserting an opaque encoding and a sorry, neither of which existed. The sharpest part is the docstring paragraph immediately following, which is CORRECT about its own predecessor: "A previous revision took the branching identity as a hypothesis h_branching on the main theorem - definitionally the conclusion - so the substantive identity was assumed rather than stated; that encoding (and its docstrings claim of a sorry that did not exist) is corrected here." That correction moved the hypothesis from a theorem argument into a class field - the same assumption under a different binder - and carried the false sorry claim forward verbatim. A documented fix that reinstated the documented defect in the commit that names it.
proof-statement-integrity.notes: Repaired to 1a disposition 3. markov_identification now derives clause (ii) from the branching identity taken as a hypothesis. Clause (i) (amplitudeEigenbasis_eq_sum) is kept and explicitly LABELLED definitional - rfl consults nothing about braids, Hecke algebras or Specht modules - so it is not mistaken for evidence about clause (ii). not_markovTrace_branching_of_free_data refutes the identity at free data, which is why a sorry would have been unsound and why a later attempt to add one fails against a standing counterexample; this is the third encoding of this lemma to claim a sorry it did not have. Verdict major not critical: the implication is derived. Open: the Wenzl-bridge decomposition tr_M = sum_lambda w_lambda tr_S_lambda itself. Nothing constructs rho_n, H_n(R,q), the Specht modules, or the quantum dimensions in w_lambda. The in-repo RSK infrastructure proves the classical Burnside identity for symmetric groups, not this branching. Verified lean-direct exit 0. Bean qou-z9ws.
